Design assumptions & research

This is an early, deliberately forgiving model. Production, prices, service capacities and compressed case durations are authored game parameters—not estimates of real economies, crime, legal procedure, or medicine. Cases are authored demonstrations; this version does not predict crime or generate incidents from demographic traits.

The town starts with jobs, households and supply arrangements. Farms and woodland appear outside its center. The marketplace receives raw materials; workshops buy them and sell finished goods; households purchase what they need. Outside supply and financial support are visible in the ledger.

Justice distinguishes a report from an established finding, supports affected people, makes restorative meetings voluntary, and preserves housing and employment during recovery or reintegration. Serious property damage demonstrates time-limited custody after independent review. No military systems.

Research references: UNODC: restorative justice values · Restorative Justice Handbook · NIJ: evidence and limitations in policing research. These inform design principles, not numerical calibration.

People reuse the project’s existing role models and animations. Buildings are an original simple town layout. Saved in this browser; no offline progression.
